title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Priya Nair
ci_summary: Initial CI run failed on unit test TestKVCacheExpiry (flaky), tests re-run after fix; subsequent pipeline completed with all checks green (lint, unit, integration, e2e).
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost for common workloads by automatically selecting batching, KV caching defaults and quantization profiles while surfacing unit-economic impact in the Optimize console. This PR wires together: 1) autotune defaults engine to propose batching/window/cache params per model+route, 2) persistent quantization-profile suggestions for model variants, and 3) unit-economics tooling to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs for rollout. Changes span runtime heuristics, control-plane storage for profiles, and UI telemetry. Checklist: - [x] implement autotune rules and default proposal API - [x] persist suggested quant profiles and exposure via model catalog - [x] add simulation endpoint for unit economics tooling - [x] update Optimize console telemetry and rollout UI hints - [x] add integration tests + e2e coverage - [x] document config knobs in docs site Notes: the description includes the proposal format and a brief rollout strategy. Rollout plan is staged: feature gate off by default, enable for 10% of traffic for eligible customers, monitor A/B regressions on quality metrics and unit-econ delta. Backwards compatibility: safe defaults retained; nothing forces quantization without explicit acceptance during staged rollout. Related: ENG-4217 implements the tuning rules; PM-298 tracks product acceptance criteria.

review_conversation: Evan Kwiatkowski: Nice work on assembling the end-to-end flow. A few questions: how do we guard against silent quality regressions when suggesting quant profiles? Can we auto-run a small eval set in CI?

Priya Nair: We added an optional CI eval hook that runs a lightweight prompt-set against proposed quantized variants and attaches a similarity/regression score to the proposal object. It's off by default for speed but enabled in our e2e pipelines for staging.
Daniela Ruiz: I see risk around batch sizing increasing latency tail for latency-sensitive routes. Can we add a per-route opt-out and a hard SLO guard?

Priya Nair: Added per-route opt-out and a runtime SLO check that prevents applying larger batch sizes when end-to-end p99 latency would exceed configured SLO. See runtime/scheduler change and control-plane guard.
Maya Chen: CI failed on TestKVCacheExpiry on first run; was that a real regression?
Priya Nair: Root cause was test race on mocked time; fixed by explicit time control and added stabilization script. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.
Evan Kwiatkowski: Approving after minor comment on telemetry naming (updated).
release_notes: Autosuggest autotune defaults for batching/caching and quantization profiles; add unit-economics simulator in Optimize console; staged rollout by feature flag. Admins can opt out per-route. See docs/autotune.md for rollout guidance.
